evaluation: bemlops time-ordered split (0.8/0.1/0.1, 1 h gaps). The deployed model is trained up to 2023-05-22 15:15, and the held-out test period 2023-05-22 16:45 to 05-31 (893 intervals) gives RMSE 27.2 ppm against 33.6 ppm for persistence (last 15-min mean known 1 h ahead; skill 0.19). Validation 05-13 to 05-22 gave 17.4 vs 19.9 ppm. I quote the test figure because the later data may include busier periods: persistence RMSE was 37-45 ppm in March-April and 28 ppm in May. predict() on train.csv reproduces the test RMSE exactly, and forecasts from copies truncated at 6 cutoffs match the full-file forecasts exactly (max difference 0 ppm).
model: bemlops HistGradientBoosting ('gbm', tuned by bemlops random search with time-ordered CV). It predicts the 1 h change of the 15-min mean CO2; the forecast is the last 15-min mean known at forecast time plus that change. Inputs, all lagged >= 1 h by bemlops: CO2 change history (t-1h..t-1h45, t-24h, t-7d, 1-day mean), CO2 level, room-active PIR, damper, light on/off, window, supply airflow, room and outdoor temperature, derived CO2 trend (30/60 min), share of the last hour the room was active, fan state and room activity at the same time of day 24 h and 7 d earlier, and fan-schedule x CO2-excess / occupancy interactions. bemlops adds hour, weekday and weekend features at the target time. If the model gives no output, the forecast falls back to persistence.
data_findings: Timestamps are ISO-8601 with DST offsets (+0100 until 2023-03-26, then +0200). I parsed them to UTC and converted to Europe/Copenhagen; forecasts are indexed in that time zone.
One full day (2023-05-24 23:05 to 05-25 23:00, 288 rows) appears twice with identical values, and 2023-04-24 13:05-15:30 is in reverse order. I averaged duplicate timestamps and sorted by time.
12 h 5 min gap on 2023-04-02 (07:40-19:45), plus scattered #N/A rows. Gaps stay missing: inputs are forward-filled for at most 1 h, the target never.

RoomB:Sensor__room_temperature switches from degC to degF on 2023-05-12 08:00 and stays in degF to the end (72-83). The loader converts any reading above 50 from degF, one reading at a time, so the rule is causal and also works if the switch persists or reverts.
Outdoor:Temperature_air has 8 isolated glitches of 57-73 degC; masked as impossible (outside -40..45). A 9.5 h flat stretch is left as is.
The target CO2 has 16 readings of -999 (masked) and two single-sample jumps (1521 ppm on 2023-04-21; kept, since a live forecast cannot know a reading is a spike until the next one arrives).

The CO2 sensor logs on change of value with a ~50 ppm deadband. It is unchanged in about 95% of 5-min steps and flat for whole weekends (e.g. 428 ppm for 3.6 days). This is real behaviour, not a stuck sensor, so I declared it flat_ok and did not mask it.
Outdoor:Wind__velocity contains the text 'OFFLINE' (12 rows). It is not used.
RoomB:People__amount is 62% missing and absent from 2023-04-18 on, so it is unusable for future forecasts and I dropped it. The three setpoints are constant (22 / 20.5 / 23.5 degC) and are not used.

Operation change: from 2023-05-04 the ventilation runs 05:00-21:00 instead of 08:00-16:15, with night flushing around 23:00 on some days, and from 2023-05-08 the window is open most of the time. With bemlops' default 0.7/0.15/0.15 split, training ended on 05-03 and no model beat persistence. That is why I used 0.8/0.1/0.1, so training includes the new schedule, and added derived inputs for the fan state 24 h / 7 d earlier at the target time of day. In exploration, the same gbm's error on 2023-05-18..31 fell from 28.3 to 24.6 ppm when the summer weeks were in its training data (persistence: 29.5).

Holidays (Easter, 05-18/19, 05-29) are inconsistent: on some the room was used, on others it was empty. The model has no holiday flag and over-predicts a little on empty holidays (e.g. 10 ppm RMSE on 2023-05-29, where persistence was exact).
Errors come mostly from weekday 08-11 (people arriving) and 16-19 (fan stop or people leaving): on the test set, weekday 07-20 RMSE is 39.7 ppm vs 49.7 for persistence, and other hours 11.3 vs 12.1.
usability: Project(df, timestamp='timestamp') crashes with pandas 'ValueError: Mixed timezones detected' on ISO timestamps whose UTC offset changes with daylight saving (+0100/+0200), which is the normal format for a European BAS export. I had to parse with utc=True and tz_convert myself. A timezone= argument, or utc=True plus conversion, would fix this; the skill's DST advice does not cover mixed offsets.

save_run() fails with 'TypeError: Start and end cannot both be tz-aware with different timezones' (report.model_card -> pd.date_range(tr0, tr1)) when the index is tz-aware Europe/Copenhagen and the training period spans a DST change. run.json, report.md, model.joblib and the plots are written, but model_card.md and anything after it are not, and the error loses the fitted model unless it was saved first. I saved it with results.model.save() instead.

prepare()'s stuck and spike masking are not causal, and ForecastModel.predict re-applies the same options to live data. I checked this on synthetic data. A genuine step change is masked as a 'spike' when it is the last reading in the file but kept once a later reading exists. A stuck stretch is masked from its start only after it has lasted stuck_hours, so a long file masks values that a short file kept. Forecasts can therefore depend on data after the forecast time, and the leakage audit (which covers features only) does not catch it. I disabled both (mask_stuck=False, mask_spikes=False) and cleaned row by row in my own loader. Causal variants for serving would help, or at least a warning.
check_data() and the live check keep saying 'prepare() treats them as missing' for spikes and stuck stretches even when the project's prepare options turn that masking off.

A unit change partway through a series (room temperature degC to degF on 2023-05-12) is reported only as out_of_range ERROR '...check the declaration'. The unit_mismatch logic that names the right unit works only for the whole column; detecting the change point ('values after <time> fit degF') would have pointed straight at the fix.

With the default split (0.7/0.15/0.15), a change in operation at the train/validation boundary made persistence win, and the only message was the generic 'look for better inputs'. A check that compares train and validation inputs (here supply airflow by hour) would explain it. The fractions= argument of fit() is undocumented (fit has no docstring); I found it from the signature.

No option to forecast the change from the last known value (a differenced target). Tree models on the level could not reproduce long flat CO2 periods. I worked around it by declaring my own change column as the target (quantity 'other'). bemlops then reports a misleading 'persistence' baseline ('the last hour's change repeats', skill 0.43) and meaningless CV(RMSE)/NMBE (the target's mean is about 0), so I computed the honest zero-change baseline myself. The declared unit 'ppm' on an 'other' column is also dropped ('RMSE 27.2 ,' with no unit).
Calendar features (hour, weekday, weekend) are always added, and there is no way to switch them off or to add a holiday calendar.

The deployed ForecastModel is trained on train+validation only (train_end = end of validation), so the newest 10% of data is never used. That matters exactly when operation has just changed. There is no simple documented way to refit the chosen configuration on all data without a Registry/retrain cycle that needs new unseen data.

ForecastModel.predict(future=True) returns forecasts for the first hour of the file, where there is no data at all (imputed medians; forecast_made_at is before the data starts). It probably also returns a forecast from a partial last 15-min interval if the file ends mid-interval (I did not check this). I trimmed the output to intervals whose input interval is complete.

Speed: 'import bemlops' took 60-90 s on this busy 8-core Windows machine (scipy.stats and sklearn are imported eagerly through bemlops.models and deploy). fit() with the three default models took about 40 min (random_forest with n_jobs=-1 inside random-search CV) and printed no progress. I left random_forest out; ridge+gbm took about 8 min. predict() still runs in about 25-30 s.

What worked well: change-of-value logging with a deadband was recognised and flat_ok=True suggested, which was exactly right here. 'OFFLINE' text, -999 placeholders, duplicate and unsorted rows and gaps were all reported clearly. Unit conversion (m3/h to m3/s) and the 'no model beat persistence' warning were useful.
